payload.title: untrusted_context_fields bounds the planner's untrusted-context block only by the 24,000-character whole-body cap, so one long reason or a long ref list cuts the JSON body mid-string, drops provenance_refs and refused_evidence_refs, and leaves a body that is not valid JSON
evidence: aria-kernel/aria_kernel/pressure_evidence.py:109-121 (the one producer: json.dumps(payload, sort_keys=True) passed whole to untrusted_block; no per-value bound)
aria-kernel/aria_kernel/pressure_evidence.py:143-152 (reason, provenance_refs and refused_evidence_refs enter the payload unbounded; sort_keys puts refused_evidence_refs last)
aria-kernel/aria_kernel/text_safety.py:79-83 (the cap truncates the already serialised and escaped body at a character count)
aria-kernel/aria_kernel/pressure.py:1063-1065 (a pressure record stores reason and provenance_refs with no length bound)

aria-kernel/aria_kernel/mission.py:507-514 (a mission's evidence_refs only grow: sorted(set(old + new)) on every opened/evidence event; pr:<n> and branch:<name> refs all land in refused_evidence_refs)

payload.rule_violated: PLAN-v2 F4.0b: the planner block has one producer; the per-field bounds it replaced (reason 1024, each ref 512) guaranteed every key survived, and the cap should be applied per value at the producer, not to the serialised text.
payload.notes: A mission whose accumulated refs serialise past about 24,000 characters (a few hundred refused pr:/branch: entries), or a pressure reason longer than that, makes untrusted_block cut the escaped JSON text at the cap. The tail of the body is the sorted-last key refused_evidence_refs, so it is dropped first, and when the cut lands inside a string the block's body is not parseable JSON; only the trailing '...[truncated]' marker tells the planner that anything is missing. At the base each field was bounded, so all three keys were always present and the body always parsed. The affected data is the planner's read-and-never-cite context, so the harm is lost provenance, not a boundary breach; the trigger is a long mission or reason, not an attacker. Close condition: In untrusted_context_fields bound each value before serialising (a per-value character cap and a list-length cap with an explicit omitted-count entry) so the serialised body stays under the block cap and parses. Add a test: a 30,000-character reason and a 3,000-ref list each give a block whose body parses as JSON and still names all three keys. Verified at origin/main ae2958653d.
